Image on the page "Smart Ozone Sterilizing Robot" (https://innowings.engg.hku.hk/sorbot/)

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster advertising a "Smart Ozone Sterilizing Robot" product/technology.

2. TEXT:
- SMART OZONE STERILIZING ROBOT
- CLOUD
- Our cloud platform is built by ASP.Net and is made for two purposes. First: for ozone concentration tracking. Air quality inside the sterilization room can be monitored to ensure that it is safe enough for humans to get in. Second: for robot location tracking, we can have real-time tracking of a robot during product delivery avoid off-tracking and losing.
- ROS
- Robot Operating System-ROS. ROS is more like a framework responsible for communicating and operating the various components of the robot. Take the walking of the robot as an example. To make the robot walk, it needs to control the motor underneath, and there are some obstacle avoidance sensors. The functions in ROS act like a bridge for the controlling programs of both motors and the sensors to communicate and coordinate.
- AGV
- Agv means automated guided vehicle which can follow the wires on the floor. Our purchased agv can be controlled by ROS language and it has vision camera for navigation. We would set the route for the agv to fit the layout of the elderly home. To avoid the collision between the agv and the elderlies, our agv will design with highly maneuverable with suitable size and moving speed.

- WE HUNT, WE EXPLORE, WE THRIVE WITH OUR BEST FRIEND: DOGS, SINCE THE DAWN OF HUMANITY.
- ADVANTAGES OF DOGGIE
- Unique combination of strength and agility
- Accompaniment of robustness with capacity
- Platform for implementing complex solutions
- Friendly incorporation into the community
- MANUFACTURING
- The latest prototype is 40x20x40mm in size and weighs 1kg. The model comprises a main body framework for accommodating electrical/battery components and 4 legs, each of 3 limbs and 3 joints

- 3D parts such as limbs were modelled in SolidWorks and printed with Polymaker PolyLite material

- A total of 12 Goolsky DSSERVO DS3218MG 20kg Metal Gear Digital Steering Servos are used for the 4 limbs
- IMPLEMENTATION OF IOT
- The ESP32 module is used as the microcontroller unit, as it contains an embedded Bluetooth module capable of initializing a BLE server and detecting Bluetooth clients (i.e. Mobile devices with our DoggiE application)
- The inertial measurement unit (IMU) comprises the Adafruit LIS3MDL+LSM303DCHCX feathering, which collects and feeds rotational and positional data into the control system
- Simulations were run on the PyBullet physics engine for proof-of-concept of both our backend algorithms (e.g. Walking and auto-balancing) and validation of our mechanical design

- WALKING, SITTING, STRETCHING
- DoggiE enjoys a wide range of motion, which enables it to perform complex tasks while maintaining balance.

- DoggiE is fully responsive to mobile control and implements the latest IoT technology by utilizing BLE networks.

2. TEXT:
- FOOD CITY PANDA RUN!
- ----- A COMP3329 Course Project
- THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG
- DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE
- Supervisor: Dr. Chim Tat Wing
- Group Members:
  ZHAO Youran (Skye)
  CHOW Stephanie
  LI Liuhao (Bowen)
  CHAU Ki Shiu (Tom)
- Introduction & Story
- FOOD City PANDA Run! is a 3D Runner Game developed during the course of COMP3329 Computer Game Design and Programming. The game idea is actually drawn from a book-keeping app called Fortune City which applies gamification of personal finance managing. We aim to apply a similar design to food delivery apps such as foodpanda, that the game can be embedded to those apps to meet business objectives as retain current customers and attract new ones.
  The background story goes as follows. In 20 AC (After Covid), Hong Kong is under a great depression of economy and food supply. To make ends meet, the player has to take a part-time job as a food delivery guy. However, in today's world, even the slightest mistake can lead people being fired, to make sure all the food reaches their customers intact, the player must avoid all obstacles appearing on their road of delivery...
- Technical Specifications and Assets Used
- FOOD City PANDA Run! is developed on Unity game engine and used c# as scripting language. All assets were purchased on unity asset store, including Hong Kong Street (for overall game scenes), Japanese School Lunch (for food choices), and Mobile Traffic System (for player car). For sound effect of the game, such as background music and coin collect effects, we referred to some online open source of audio materials. Some sample game scenes and assets are shown below:
- Player View of Roads, coins and Obstacles
- Player Car with Food
- Road Barrier as Obstacle
- Game Logic
  1. The player initially has 3 food on the tray for delivery.
  2. The player can move Left or Right by pressing ← and →, or A and D, to avoid hitting the obstacles and to collect coins as delivery tips.
  3. If the player have a minor or indirect collision (like pushing) with the obstacle, it will push the obstacle away without punishment.
  4. The food will drop from the tray if the player hit directly with the obstacle. The number of food that drops depends on how hard the player hit the obstacle.
  5. The player fails the game if there is no food left on the tray.

1. WHAT IT IS: Academic conference-style research poster about a final year project on weakly supervised localization for assembly line understanding.

2. TEXT:
- Title: Weakly Supervised Localization for Assembly Line Understanding
- Supervisor: Prof. Wenping WANG
- Second Examiner: Dr. Jia PAN
- Jiarui WANG(3035332153) Yafei YANG(3035331501)
- FYP19015
- Headings: Background; Our Architecture; Experiment Result; Methodology; Data Set; Summary & Future work; References
- Background bullets: 1. Object Localization: Find where the object is and draw a bounding box around it. 2. Weakly Supervised Localization: Training data does not have localization guidance. 3. Our Task: Localize object being operated on assembly line in a weakly supervised manner.
- Our Architecture bullets: 1. Classification Sub-network Extracted deep feature from input image 2. Attention Proposal Sub-network Take in feature maps and generate parameters for image cropping. 3. Generate CAM: Map back weights from fully connected layer to the feature maps extracted.
- Methodology bullets: 1. Class Activation Map Visualize discriminative region used by classifier to make the prediction. • Different region is activated for different label prediction • Activation region is responsible for the corresponding prediction. 2. Recurrent Attention CNN Stack multiple CNNs to gradually focus on the most representative area. • Different classification network at different scale; • Additional module predict attended region to zoom in.
- Data Set bullets: label: Hard Drive, Power Supply and CD Rom • 7342 training images, 399 testing images
- Experiment Result bullets: For the baseline testing, we achieved 99.25% accuracy. For localization, we achieved 86.72% 0.25 recall rate. Apart from the base model, we evaluate the effect of data set processing, temporal loss, lr range and APN structure.
- Summary & Future work bullets: We implemented a new model with both CNN visualization and finer scale rescaling. we achieved 99.25% accuracy for classification, 86.72% 0.25 recall rate for localization. Implement APN with 3 stacked layers. Collect validation dataset and fine tune hyper-parameters. Compare with state-of-the-art's claimed accuracy.

2. TEXT:
Title: HELPING LOW-INCOME TENANTS IN HONG KONG WITH COMPUTER VISION
The Problem
• Tenants' rights are disorganised and confusing.
• Tenants avoid suing their landlords in fear of being kicked out, which means that their rights in law are not enforced.
• Disconnection between tenants and those responsible for protecting their rights since it is difficult to report and detect breaches

Our Solution
• Database of regulations on health and safety.
• Computer vision: our platform recognises objects and links them to the relevant health and safety provisions.
• Reporting breaches: our platform has the contact details of those in charge of rectifying each specific breach in order to better connect tenants with the authorities. Tenants can also create an anonymous report to avoid being punished by landlords.

ProperT

Image on the page "A Smart Robotic Walker with Intelligent Close-proximity Interaction Capabilities for Elderly Mobility Safety" (https://innoacademy.engg.hku.hk/smartwalker/)

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster describing a research project on a smart robotic walker for elderly mobility safety.

2. TEXT:
- Title: A Smart Robotic Walker with Intelligent Close-proximity Interaction Capabilities for Elderly Mobility Safety
- PC: Prof. Chuan Wu, Department of Computer Science, The University of Hong Kong
- Sections/headings and short lines shown:
  - We propose a novel smart robotic walker that targets a convenient-to-use indoor walking aid for the elderly. The walker supports multiple modes of interactions through voice, gait or haptic touch, and allows intelligent control via learning-based methods to achieve mobility safety.
  - Recovery Support: Our walker provides stable support for users to recovery from abnormal status such as fallen and sitting, through the cooperation of brake and soft interface.
  - Sound Source Localization: Walker extracts time-delay feature from voice signal and navigates to the summoning user through RL-based SSL technique.
  - Soft Interface: Soft robotic handles with haptic monitor detect user intention and emergency events.
  - Front Following: A built-in DNN observes lower limb gesture obtained from Lidar and IR, and tracks user in front while providing walking safety support.
  - Motion System: Differential driver and emergency brake guarantee the flexibility and safety.
  - Falling Protection: Soft interface detects abnormal force pressure and activates brake to provide safety support.

3. COLOURS: Predominantly blue background with cyan and white text boxes and orange accents on walker handles.

4. PEOPLE AND OBJECTS: Silhouettes of three human figures and three robotic walker illustrations; additional icons showing sensors, wheels, and path/navigation diagrams.

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster for an engineering course group project showcasing a smart soccer robot called "The Charging Bull".
2. TEXT:
   - ENGG1320 IMSE GROUP D4
   - SMART SOCCER ROBOT - "THE CHARGING BULL"
   - Innovative Bull-shaped Design
   - Interlocking Mechanisms
   - Foul-counting
   - Quick Fabrication
   - Sturdy Construction
   - The design of the robot is based on a charging bull, with the horns capable of capturing the ball. This design makes the robot more appealing to school children receiving STEM education, which is our target audience.
   - The wooden panels are held together by interlocking mechanisms. This makes the assembly process fun and simple, without the use of glue or tape. A few screws are still needed to secure the electronics.
   - The robot includes an optical "line follower", the seven segment display on the back displays the number of times a black line is crossed. A reset button is included, so the count can be reset without restarting the robot.
   - The wooden panels are produced by laser cutting, while the wheels are made by 3D printing. The holes in the wheels make them lightweight and quick to print.
   - The robot is made up of many interlocking plates, which protects the internal electronics. It would not break easily during a match.
   - A honeycomb pattern of holes on the back allows the remote IR signals to reach the sensor on the mCore.

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster describing a university engineering project titled "Automatic Chair Parking System."

2. TEXT:
- Automatic Chair Parking System
- The University of Hong Kong
- Department of Mechanical Engineering
- BACKGROUND
- The Automatic Chair Parking System aims to provide a smart solution in classroom and other similar environment by helping to move and arrange chairs, while reducing the risk of occupational injuries and potential dangers related to the repetitive works. This can also reduce the reliance on labor force and ultimately improve the efficiency. The system therefore is designed to autonomously transport chairs to the designated parking area with minimal human control.
- OBJECTIVE
- The system will be a four-wheeled vehicle that provides the following operations:
  1. Generate a map of the surrounding in an unknown environment
  2. Search for and identify the chairs in the vicinity
  3. Autonomously plan a path to reach the chair
  4. Orientate the vehicle itself under the chair;
  5. Lift the chair up and transport the chair to a designated parking or storage area.
- FUNCTIONS
- Navigation
- Searching
- Lifting
- Chassis

Image on the page "Investigation of Influencing Factors on the Engineering Properties of Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation (MICP) Treated Soils" (https://innowings.engg.hku.hk/influencing-factors-soils/)

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster about an academic CIVL4102 Project on Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation treated soils.

2. TEXT:
Title: Investigation of Influencing Factors On Engineering Properties of Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation Treated Soils

Department of Civil Engineering
The University of Hong Kong
CIVL4102 Project
Timothy Ting
Supervisor: Dr. Man Man Hu

Background
- Soil improvement: modify and enhance soil’s engineering properties
- Conventional techniques: soil compaction, preloading, chemical grouting
- Chemical grouts may potentially damage the environment due to release of toxic chemicals (e.g. acrylamides) [1]
- Bio-grouting - Emerging Alternative: environmentally friendly, economical [1]
Microbially Induced Calcite Precipitation (MICP): A Promising Bio-grouting Technique

Bacteria and chemical solution (urea and calcium ions) injected into soil
Bacteria hydrolyze urea into carbonate ions [2]
CO(NH2)2 + 2H2O → 2NH4+ + CO32-
Calcite binds soil grains together, enhancing soil’s engineering properties
Carbonate ions combine with calcium ions to precipitate as calcite in soil pores [2]
Ca2+ + CO32- → CaCO3 (s)

Objectives and Methodology
- Investigate the effects of several influencing factors on the engineering properties of the MICP-treated silica sand
- Influencing factors:
  ⇨ Injected chemical concentration
  ⇨ Retention time of injection
  ⇨ Relative density
  ⇨ Sand particle size distribution
- Conduct laboratory tests to determine the unconfined compressive strength (UCS) and permeability of the MICP-treated sand

After MICP treatment:
- Calcite content determination
- Microscopic calcite precipitation patterns

Task List
- Sample preparation of a target size distribution
- Determination of max and min void ratios
- Investigation of effects of influencing factors
- Effect of calcite content on permeability & UCS

Expected Results
- Low chemical injection concentration → smaller crystals of uniform sizes precipitate evenly over sand particle surfaces, vice versa for higher concentrations [3]
- Increasing calcite precipitation → general decrease in permeability and increase in UCS [3]

Potential MICP Applications [2][4][5]
- Land reclamation
- Reduce ground settlement and soil erosion
- Resist against soil liquefaction
- Stabilize slopes and embankments
- Increase foundation bearing capacity

Image captions visible:
- Experimental setup for MICP treatment
- Pure silica sand before MICP treatment
- MICP-treated silica sand

1. WHAT IT IS: Academic conference-style poster about a final year project on weakly supervised localization for assembly line understanding.

2. TEXT:
Title: Weakly Supervised Localization for Assembly Line Understanding
Supervisor: Prof. Wenping WANG
Second Examiner: Dr. Jia PAN
Jiarui WANG(3035332153) Yafei YANG(3035331501)
FYP19015

Headings: Background; Our Architecture; Experiment; Methodology; Data Set; Summary & Future work; References

Background bullets: 1. Object Localization: Find where the object is and draw a bounding box around it. 2. Weakly Supervised Localization: Training data does not have localization guidance. 3. Our Task: Localize object being operated on assembly line in a weakly supervised manner.

Our Architecture bullets: 1. Classification Sub-network Extracted deep feature from input image. 2. Attention Proposal Sub-network Take in feature maps and generate parameters for image cropping. 3. Generate CAM: Map back weights from fully connected layer to the feature maps extracted.

Data Set: label: Hard Drive, Power Supply and CD Rom; 7342 training images, 399 testing images

Experiment bullets include: For the baseline testing, we achieved 99.25% accuracy. For localization, we achieved 86.72% 0.25 recall rate. Table and figure captions: Figure4. Statistics result for base model; Figure2: Overall Architecture of Model; Figure3. Example training data from three classes; Figure1. Class Activation Map for Different Class; Table 1. Summary of Experiment Result

Summary & Future work bullets include: We implemented a new model with both CNN visualization and finer scale rescaling. we achieved 99.25% accuracy for classification, 86.72% 0.25 recall rate for localization. Implement APN with 3 stacked layers. Collect validation dataset and fine tune hyper-parameters. Compare with state-of-the-art’s claimed accuracy

References: [1] Bolei Zhou, Aditya Khosla, Agata Lapedriza, Aude Oliva, and Antonio Torralba. Learning deep features for discriminative localization. In Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, pages 2921–2929, 2016. [2] Jianlong Fu, Heliang Zheng, and Tao Mei. Look closer to see better: Recurrent attention convolutional neural network for fine-grained image recognition. In Proceedings of the IEEE conference on computer vision and pattern recognition, pages 4438–4446, 2017.

- According to a survey conducted in 2015 that focused on 500 students, the following results were recorded:
- In order to tackle this issue, we present to you Drift Bottle, an innovative platform for students to express their emotions in a message-in-a-bottle style!!!
- 46.70% Others

Slide3
1. WHAT IT IS: Slide (presentation) outlining objectives for a student mental-health sharing platform.

2. TEXT:
- Objectives
- Allowing anonymous sharing of stressed thoughts by students to help them express their emotions
- Expressing negative emotions in a story-telling way to relieve stress
- Posting positive stories to inspire others and bring a smile to the community
- Providing support from expertise that could talk with and guide students who might be having negative thoughts

3. COLOURS: Pale blue gradient background with darker teal-blue text and aqua sea-toned band at the bottom; yellow emoji accents.

Slide4
1. WHAT IT IS: presentation slide about "Inspirations and Comparisons to Past Works" comparing QQ and WeChat with Drift Bottle.

2. TEXT:
- Inspirations and Comparisons to Past Works
- QQ and WeChat (漂流瓶)
  - Anonymous sharing of messages
  - Able to reply messages
  - Able to add writer as friend
  - Misused for advertisement and pornography
  - Services stopped in May–June 2019
- Drift Bottle
  - Anonymous sharing of stories
  - Not able to comment on stories; instead, simple feedback system is provided
  - Normal user is not able to contact writer, but specialist could approach him and provide guidance
  - AI adopted to carry out content moderation and prevent various kinds of malicious content

3. COLOURS: pale aqua and light blue gradient background with teal text and ocean-blue accents.

2. TEXT: 
Title: AI Checking
After letter has been submitted, the story will be checked against an AI for content moderation and sentiment analysis
• Content moderation is used to filter out malicious content
• Sentiment analysis is used to determine what mood the story belongs to
• Both are text classification problems -> 2 distinct models are trained with machine learning to solve them
• Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) with TensorFlow is employed for the training

On the left are Alex and Andrew of 4ocean, who have cleaned a mammoth 5 million pounds of ocean plastic in just 2 years. And on the right are Ketut and Wahyu, who belong to the community of volunteers who clean the Canggu beach every morning on their surfboards. Now this burgeoning startup and this indigenous community, both collect ocean waste with small nets and their bare hands. And we felt that ClearBot could really scale up their efforts. Another challenge we’ve learned in Bali was that just one robot alone is not going to have the range and capacity needed to make a tangible dent in cleaning up even a small beach.  

That’s why ClearBot will rely on a system approach where a swarm of simple robots that collect trash until they reach their capacity of run out of battery. At that point, the robot goes into hibernation and sends out beacons of its location so a team of volunteer can collect the robots AND the trash back to shore for sorting. - Title: FLY ON THE GROUND! - HKU'S 1st USER-FRIENDLY WIND TUNNEL
- Authored by Chan Lok Him Justin, Sum Ku Ting / Supervised by Dr. Alan Tsang
- Section headings: FUN FACTS; APPLICATIONS; METHODOLOGY; ACCURACY
- Fun facts bullets: The Wright Brothers tested their wings in a simple wind tunnel before making history. All fleets of air and spacecrafts, even SpaceX's Starship & Falcons, are wind-tunnel tested. Professional small and portable wind tunnels cost from a staggering 50k to 300k USD. Wind tunnels are conducive to investigating aerodynamics and fluid dynamics topics!
- Applications bullets: Bridge the affordability and availability gap of for undergraduate T&L, R&D purposes. Currently applied to conduct advance airfoil and fundamental flow visualization studies. Hope our successful built can encourage HKU to semi-self-build a cost-effective wind tunnel. Ultimately Professors, Students (URFP, REU), SIGs (DBF, HKUR) can model-test in house!
- Methodology bullets: Dimensions from Hernandez et al.'s design methodology book. Honeycomb -> Contraction Cone -> Test Section -> Diffuser -> Fan housing. Design -> Build -> Embedd Systems -> Assembly -> Tests -> Investigations
- Methodology image captions: Test Objects; Mechanical System; Electrical System; Final Assembly
- Accuracy bullets: First Test: Flat Plate Aerodynamics, Our Wind Tunnel vs Published Experiments. Second Test: NACA 4415 & Optimization, Our Wind Tunnel vs Ansys, XFOIL. Third Test: Flow Visualization, Our Wind Tunnel vs UW's Kirsten Wind Tunnel
- Accuracy image captions: Flat Plate Test - Trend closely followed; Optimization Test - Error Mostly ~ 8%; Flow Test - Lam / Tur Resemblance

Another challenge we’ve learned in Bali was that just one robot alone is not going to have the range and capacity needed to make a tangible dent in cleaning up even a small beach.  

That’s why ClearBot will rely on a system approach where a swarm of simple robots that collect trash until they reach their capacity of run out of battery. At that point, the robot goes into hibernation and sends out beacons of its location so a team of volunteer can collect the robots AND the trash back to shore for sorting. 1. WHAT IT IS: Poster advertising a 2-day beginner workshop on robot control firmware.

2. TEXT:
- Title/headings: "2-DAY BEGINNER WORKSHOP: ROBOT CONTROL — FIRMWARE"
- Body excerpt: "Firmware is the software program in MCU (micro controller unit) to control the actuators such as servos and motors, and sensors of a robot. It is a challenge to develop a good firmware as MCU is not powerful as computer CPU. As MCU program runs in single thread model, programming techniques are required to efficiently coordinate each module (sensor or actuator) to avoid them from blocking each other. In this two-day workshop, you will learn the essential knowledge on writing firmware and apply what you have learnt to write the firmware for a wheel driven robot - WheeBot."

1. WHAT IT IS: Poster advertising a WebGPU programming workshop on campus.

2. TEXT:
- Title: WebGPU Workshop
- Subtitle: Synthetic Animation & Simulation in the Browser
- Logos/headers: Innovation Academy Faculty of Engineering, HKU; GDG On Campus HKU
- RSVP Now!
- Join us for an exciting WebGPU programming workshop!
- Body excerpt: This workshop will introduce you to traditional graphics programming and the power of general purpose GPU programming which powers AI neural networks. WebGPU is a work in progress standard by the W3C to enable high-performance computing on the browser through native GPU access, it is one of the major tech behind WebAI – the tech that allows running AI models in your browser. By the end of the workshop, you'll have learned to create a dynamic and responsive particle effect graphics on a webpage.
- Event details: date: 22 Sep 2025 (Mon), time: 17:00 - 19:00, location: HKU Inno Wing Digital Learning Studio
- Side note: We are also looking for HKU students interested in joining our Google Developer Group, where you will be able to meet other like minded people across the GDG community!

4. PEOPLE AND OBJECTS: Main objects: WebGPU logo and large black rounded rectangle with colored particle animation graphic, QR code, Innovation Academy and GDG logos, decorative icons and punctuation marks (about 8 decorative symbols). No people visible.

- Unleash Creativity with Generative AI through Open AI Engine and ChatGPT
- Build Your Personalized Chatbot
- In this interactive workshop, you'll harness the capabilities of the ChatGPT engine to create a personalized chatbot tailored to your needs. We'll guide you through the concept of generative AI, data preparation, using the Azure OpenAI API, chatbot development, avatar generation, and the seamless integration of speech-to-text and text-to-speech services to deliver dynamic user experiences. Don't miss this opportunity to elevate your creative potential with generative AI!
